mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing liquidity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate signals labor market weakness, which may indicate broader economic slowdowns, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE rises by >0.3pp, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is rising and the unemployment rate is falling, it may signal a tightening labor market and potential monetary policy tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS is rising and UNRATE is falling, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong consumer demand and economic expansion, which tends to boost equity markets, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods when HOUST is increasing, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 95 index points signals supply-side weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO is below 95, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth during an economic expansion indicates strong aggregate demand, which tends to boost equity markets, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of periods when GDPC1 is growing, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When employment (PAYEMS) increases but the unemployment rate (UNRATE) also rises, it may indicate labor market inefficiencies or unexpected economic conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of periods when PAYEMS increases and UNRATE also rises, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 230 may signal inflationary pressures, leading to potential monetary policy tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 230, this hypothesis is rejected.
